w: Mikolaj Spytek Ligeza raised a motte-and-bailey castle here in the late 1500s, expanded by 1620 into a 'palazzo in fortezza', later passing by marriage to the Lubomirskis. Austrians made it a courthouse and prison in 1820, then it was demolished and rebuilt by 1906 - only the gatehouse and bastions are original.
s: A Lubomirski castle rebuilt as a courthouse and prison
_facts: Founded by Mikolaj Spytek Ligeza, late 16th century
Expanded into a 'palazzo in fortezza' by 1620
Used as an Austrian courthouse and prison from 1820
Rebuilt 1902-1906; only the gatehouse and bastions are original

w: Its centerpiece, Wiezowiec W, rises 220.67 meters - the third-tallest building in Poland and, notably, the tallest residential tower in the country, having overtaken every previous record holder. A mixed-use complex built around one record-breaking spire on Rzeszow's skyline.
_facts: Tallest residential building in the country
